summary: Composite risk rose 0.64 to 49.02, leaving the one-week trend at 5.81 and the one-month trend at 6.66 while the level stayed inside the caution band and the regime held at goldilocks on low volatility, positive momentum and healthy breadth. The advance is not tape-confirmed. The two rates extremes that anchored the past two weeks both slipped off the top of their distribution on a fresh 2026-09-25 vintage, the 10Y at 5.17 from 5.18 and the real rate at 2.83 from 2.85, both now in the 99.92nd percentile; the front end eased 6 bp with the 2Y at 4.81 from 4.87 and the curve steepened to 0.36. Credit went the other way, with HY OAS at 2.93 from 2.80 and IG OAS at 0.81 from 0.79, which flipped the liquidity and credit block from rising to falling at 50.24. The last completed US session de-rated AI hardware broadly, with 19 of 22 themes lower and only cybersecurity, robotics and memory positive, AMD at -3.6091 and TSLA at -3.9397 against NVDA at 1.6839, yet the tracked A-share panel closed 10 of 11 names higher, led by 688825.sh at 3.2528 percent and 603986.sh at 2.5271 percent. The pre-market view therefore turns on two offsetting forces: a discount-rate constraint that has begun to ease at the margin, and an equity tape that is narrowing underneath a rising score.

top_risk_drivers.claim: The discount-rate block remains the binding constraint: the 10Y at 5.17 sits in the 99.92nd percentile with a risk score of 99.84, and the real rate at 2.83 sits in the 99.92nd percentile with a risk score of 99.92.
Macro is the heaviest of the six blocks at 69.8 and the one whose trend turned to rising, with the dollar index at 120.33 (42.9th percentile) still mid-range rather than depressed.
Equity structure deteriorated while the composite rose: breadth above MA200 fell to 0.5484 and the new-lows ratio rose to 0.129, while the new-highs ratio at 0.0065 carries a risk score of 88.7.

Credit widened rather than confirming the equity bid: HY OAS moved to 2.93 from 2.80 and IG OAS to 0.81 from 0.79, flipping the liquidity and credit block from rising to falling at 50.24. HY OAS carries the single heaviest indicator weight in that block and contributes 3.4144.

The liquidity cushion was refilled at the expense of reserves: RRP rose to 0.851 from 0.576 (6.91st percentile, risk score 86.18, contributing 3.4472) while reserve balances fell to 2930193 from 3013794 and the Treasury general account rose to 977084 from 877028 against a Fed balance sheet of 6747704.

supporting_signals.claim: The front end of the curve eased 6 bp on the 2026-09-25 vintage, with the 2Y at 4.81 from 4.87 while the 10Y held at 5.17 from 5.18, steepening the 10Y/2Y spread to 0.36 from a risk score of 36.52.

The tracked A-share panel closed 10 of 11 names higher, led by 688825.sh at 3.2528 percent and 603986.sh at 2.5271 percent, with 002156.sz at 2.4788 percent and 688008.sh at 1.9175 percent; 301308.sz was the sole decliner at -0.109 percent.
The composite rose 0.64 to 49.02 with a one-week trend of 5.81 and a one-month trend of 6.66, and the regime held at goldilocks on low volatility, positive momentum and healthy breadth.
Crypto turned positive, with Bitcoin at 84030, Ethereum at 2711.45 and Solana at 119.38.
The dollar index at 120.33 (42.9th percentile) remains the one macro input far from a cycle extreme, while the 10Y and the real rate both sit at the 99.92nd percentile.

contradicting_signals.claim: The last completed US session de-rated AI broadly: 19 of 22 themes closed lower, with only cybersecurity at 0.7132, robotics at 1.2484 and memory at 0.3781 positive, while AI software fell to -3.0683, AI infrastructure to -2.7242 and data centers to -2.6711.
Among the five tracked US mega-caps only NVDA advanced, at 1.6839, against AMD at -3.6091, TSLA at -3.9397, MU at -2.6149 and AVGO at -0.9183.

Cross-asset confirmation printed 0.5, so only 5 of the 10 tracked signals triggered, and because that indicator carries the largest effective weight it contributes 7.5 to the composite, more than any single input; the block's own trend is flat.

The volatility block's low reading rests on a stale observation: the layer's VIX print is dated 2026-09-22 at 14.21 (15.56th percentile, risk score 15.56), so the 15.01 volatility score is built on a value several sessions old rather than the most recent close.

Neither classic confirmation is present: credit widened and breadth above MA200 narrowed to 0.5484 while the composite rose to 49.02, so the advance rests on the rate block easing at the margin rather than on risk appetite improving.

what_changed_today: The composite rose 0.64 to 49.02; the caution risk level and the goldilocks regime were both unchanged.

The rates block rolled to a 2026-09-25 observation: the 10Y at 5.17 from 5.18, the 2Y at 4.81 from 4.87 and the real rate at 2.83 from 2.85, with both extremes dropping below the 100.0th percentile for the first time in several sessions.
Credit widened to HY OAS 2.93 from 2.80 and IG OAS 0.81 from 0.79, and the liquidity and credit block flipped from a rising to a falling trend at 50.24.
The tracked A-share panel closed 10 of 11 names higher, led by 688825.sh at 3.2528 percent, 603986.sh at 2.5271 percent and 002156.sz at 2.4788 percent, with only 301308.sz lower at -0.109 percent.
Reserve balances fell to 2930193 from 3013794 while the RRP facility refilled to 0.851 from 0.576 and the Treasury general account rose to 977084 from 877028.
Crypto flipped positive, with Bitcoin at 84030, Ethereum at 2711.45 and Solana at 119.38, and Bitcoin dominance at 0.587926.

Overnight corporate flow stayed AI-financing heavy: Nvidia added $150B to its buyback authorisation, Samsung and its five affiliates committed $1B to the KKR-launched Helix vehicle, and Nvidia's agreed purchase of Hugging Face was reported at roughly $13B, with Citi lifting its estimate of Nvidia revenue per GW to as much as $40B from $18B.
watch_next: The 2026-09-29 JOLTS print, then the 2026-09-30 Personal Income and Outlays and GDP releases, both flagged high importance; the 2026-10-02 Employment Situation closes the week.
Payrolls at 162.0 against a prior 21.0 leave the labour data as the main test of whether the 6 bp front-end easing extends into the long end.

Policy pricing still points to another hike: the fed funds implied rate is 4.205 against an effective rate of 3.88, with overnight press flow putting the next move at 65 percent and the following one near 80 percent and a cumulative 88 bp of tightening over the coming year.
Whether the 10Y and the real rate, now at the 99.92nd percentile after being pinned at the 100.0th, keep backing away from the top of their range.
Whether credit widening continues: HY OAS at 2.93 and IG OAS at 0.81 are the two inputs that would turn this score advance into a genuine risk event.

Whether the volatility block receives a current observation: the VIX series is dated 2026-09-22, so any fresh print materially above 14.21 would invalidate the low volatility reading behind the goldilocks regime.

China policy flow: the central bank cut the rate on pledged supplementary lending and the authorities launched a residential mortgage interest subsidy effective 2026-10-01, both of which sit outside the top news window and are therefore described qualitatively rather than with figures.

bull_case.title: Bull case: the discount-rate constraint keeps easing
points: The 2Y at 4.81 from 4.87 and the real rate at 2.83 from 2.85 show the first genuine front-end relief in weeks; labour and inflation data in the coming week would extend it.
The tracked A-share panel is absorbing the global AI de-rate rather than transmitting it, closing 10 of 11 names higher with 688825.sh at 3.2528 percent and 603986.sh at 2.5271 percent leading.
Crypto turned positive with Bitcoin at 84030 and the dollar index at 120.33 sits mid-range, leaving room for a broader repair in risk appetite.

base_case.title: Base case: caution holds while the score grinds higher
points: The composite holds in the 45 to 55 band with the caution level intact, consistent with a one-week trend of 5.81 and a one-month trend of 6.66.
The discount-rate block stays binding: the 10Y at 5.17 and the real rate at 2.83 remain in the 99.92nd percentile, with the curve at 0.36.
Credit and equity structure stay unconfirmed, with HY OAS at 2.93 and breadth above MA200 at 0.5484, so the advance remains a rate story rather than a risk-appetite story.

bear_case.title: Bear case: credit turns and breadth breaks
points: HY OAS at 2.93 from 2.80 is the first genuine widening impulse in weeks; a move through 3.00 would make the 50.24 liquidity and credit block the binding constraint.
Breadth above MA200 at 0.5484 and the new-lows ratio at 0.129 are already deteriorating while the score rises; a further leg lower would expose the 53.85 equity structure block.
If the volatility block receives a current VIX print and it lands materially above 14.21, the 15.01 volatility score would rise from the lowest of the six blocks into contention.
